question: Run lacunar segmentation on {volume_relative_path}. Compute the total lacunar volume as a fraction of the total bone volume (Lc.V/BV). Report in percentage.
additional_instructions: Total lacunar volume = sum of all voxels labeled as lacunae. Total bone volume = sum of voxels in the bone mask (Otsu-thresholded). Both should use the same voxel size. Use voxel size = 0.0016 mm (1.6 μm) per voxel side (voxel volume = (1.6 μm)³ ≈ 4.096 μm³).
output_instructions: Return a JSON object with keys 'lacunar_volume_um3' (float), 'bone_volume_um3' (float), 'lc_v_bv_percent' (float).
rationale: Lc.V/BV is a standard histomorphometric parameter; plausible range check catches gross segmentation errors.

question: Compute the lacunar number density (N.Lc/BV) for {volume_relative_path}: number of lacunae per mm³ of bone volume.
additional_instructions: N.Lc/BV = n_lacunae / bone_volume_mm3. Convert bone volume from voxels to mm³ using voxel_size. Report in lacunae/mm³. Use voxel size = 0.0016 mm (1.6 μm) per voxel side (voxel volume = (1.6 μm)³ ≈ 4.096 μm³).

rationale: N.Lc/BV is a standard parameter in bone histomorphometry and the primary readout of osteocyte density.

question: Compute the average distance between nearest-neighbor lacunae centroids in {volume_relative_path}. Report mean, std, and minimum nearest-neighbor distance in μm.

rationale: Nearest-neighbor distance is a standard spatial analysis metric that also serves as a quality check (very small distances = touching objects = likely over-segmentation).
